# ethereum-optimism/specs Weekly Report (Mar 1 - 7, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week’s activity on the Optimism specifications repository was focused on precision and documentation refinement within the protocol's pruning mechanisms. The primary effort centered on clarifying technical metrics for the "Holocene" upgrade, ensuring that channel size definitions are unambiguous for implementers. While the overall volume of changes was low, the focus remains on maintaining high-quality technical standards for the evolving OP Stack.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Protocol Specification Refinement
The technical work this week focused on improving the clarity of the pruning specifications, which are critical for managing node storage and data availability efficiency.
*   **Holocene Pruning Metrics:** Work began on refining how channel size metrics are defined within the pruning specification. This ensures that as the protocol evolves through the Holocene upgrade, node operators and developers have a clear mathematical and technical understanding of data lifecycle management. This was initiated via PR [#894](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/894).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

*   **Closed Issues:** No issues were closed during this period.
*   **New & Active Issues:** No new issues were reported, and there were no active discussions exceeding the three-comment threshold. The repository maintained a stable state as contributors focused on the open specification PR.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Collaboration this week was concentrated on the review and refinement of the Holocene pruning specifications. The opening of PR [#894](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/894) indicates ongoing internal maintenance and a commitment to documentation accuracy. The lack of new issues suggests a period of focused development on existing protocol roadmaps rather than the emergence of new bugs or feature requests.
